answer: The nectar multiplier is published, charged in comet, and orchard lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4204 identities would post 1896 proofs and burn roughly 70 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
